query: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy is a solid refrigeration working medium that exhibits a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor load-bearing integrity and tends to crack. What single intervention could increase its integrity while preserving caloric performance in these operating regimes? State one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its proposed mechanism, predicted integrity and caloric outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, applicable field, pressure, temperature, and loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with explicit results that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: A minor boron addition (on the order of 0.5–1.0 at%) to the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy, introduced via arc melting and homogenization, will improve grain boundary cohesion and reduce cracking under mechanical and pressure loads while retaining comparable magnetocaloric and elastocaloric performance under fields up to ~2 T and pressures up to ~200 MPa near room temperature.
generation.material_initial_state: Arc-melted and homogenized (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy exhibiting high caloric response but prone to intergranular fracture.
generation.intervention: Introduce a small boron addition before arc melting (0.5–1.0 at% B) followed by homogenization heat treatment.
generation.conditions: Field strengths up to 2 T and pressures up to ~200 MPa in a temperature range suitable for magnetocaloric and mechanocaloric operation near ambient conditions.
generation.structural_mediator: Boron segregation at grain boundaries promoting enhanced cohesion.
generation.mechanism: Boron reduces grain-boundary energy and mitigates crack initiation and propagation, leaving the magnetocaloric-active phase transitions largely unaffected.
generation.predicted_outcome: Mechanical integrity and fracture resistance are improved with little or no loss of nominal caloric performance compared to the undoped material.
generation.baseline: Undoped (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy with known large caloric effects but susceptibility to cracking under load.
generation.boundary: Suitable for operation within ~2 T and ~200 MPa at temperatures near ambient. Excessive B additions or drastically altered heat treatments could degrade or alter phase formation and caloric characteristics beyond the scope of current evidence.
generation.uncertainty: No direct studies of boron doping in (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 are found in the provided records, so the exact optimum boron content and the full influence on magnetic/pressure-driven transitions remain to be determined experimentally.

falsification_experiment.design: Produce two alloys under identical casting and heat treatment conditions: one baseline (undoped) and one with 0.5–1.0 at% boron. Compare their microstructures, mechanical strength, and caloric parameters under repeated magnetic/pressure cycling.
measurements: Fracture toughness or compressive strength tests
Adiabatic temperature change (ΔTad) under up to 2 T
Isothermal entropy change (ΔS) under up to 2 T
Volume change or stress-strain response under up to 200 MPa
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the boron-doped alloy does not exhibit any measurable increase in resistance to cracking, or if the magnetocaloric or mechanocaloric effects degrade more than ~10%, the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: FeCrNiCu based high entropy alloy matrix composites were fabricated with addition of Si and C by vacuum electromagnetic induction melting. The primary goal of this research was to analyze the reaction mechanism, microstructure, mechanical properties at room temperature and strengthening mechanism of the composites with addition of Si and C. The reaction mechanism of powders containing (Si, Ni and C) was analyzed, only one reaction occurred (i.e., Si + C → SiC) and its activation energy is 1302.8 kJ/mol. The new composites consist of a face centered cubic (FCC) structured matrix reinforced by submicron sized SiC particles. The addition of Si and C enhances the hardness from 351.4 HV to 626.4 HV and the tensile strength from 565.5 MPa to 846.0 MPa, accompanied by a slight decrease in the plasticity. The main strengthening mechanisms of SiC/FeCrNiCu composites were discussed based on dislocation strengthening, load bearing effect, Orowan mechanism and solid solution hardening, whose contributions to the tensile strength increase are 58.6%, 6.3%, 14.3% and 20.8%, respectively.
